title: Build Your Landing Page
lede: Your offer becomes a headline, one mechanism line and an application. Qualified applicants then choose a time.
deliverable: A compact landing page, progressive application and qualified booking page, with each connection tested before launch.
body:
This lesson turns the offer you already created into a page a business owner can understand quickly. By the end, you will have the landing page, the application and the page where qualified applicants book. The thank-you page comes after a real booking and is built in the next lesson.

The page is simple

Call out the buyer. Put the result they want in the headline, with the timeframe and guarantee you can honour. Use one short line underneath to explain how the service works. Then the VSL and one button: see if you qualify.

The headline is not your whole service description. Keep the deeper explanation in the video. No extra pain essay, process cards or FAQ wall beneath it.

Give Jarvis the job

Run the landing page skill for my offer. Domain: [yourdomain.com]. Calendar: [your booking link]. Video: [link, or "none yet"].

Jarvis reads your saved offer. If you have no video, it builds the Offer Testing Landing Page without a video area. If you specifically want a VSL draft before filming, tell it to leave “Insert VSL here”.

The application

Three or four useful questions about the business, one at a time. Name, email and phone go together at the end. The final step says complete your application, not choose a call.

Approved fit rules decide who can book. Qualified applicants see Congratulations, you qualify. Then: book a time to see how we can [the result]. Include the booking calendar section. Use your real calendar embed and a fallback booking link. If Jarvis does not have the URL, supply it before calling scheduling ready; a local review can show the reserved integration area.

If the answers need review, say that. Don’t approve everyone or claim a lead was saved when the form has no connected submission service. A local template is a layout example, not a working CRM.

Check the whole route

Read the page as the buyer. Test every question, Back, missing answers and a failed submission. Then test a qualified, review-needed and outside-scope application with the actual connection. Book a test slot and check that the calendar event exists. Only that booking should trigger the next page and reminders.
